rationale: Because prstkc/(dvt+prstkc) = 1 − dvt/(dvt+prstkc) and IND_ZSCORE is affine-invariant, this expression is (up to winsorization noise) the exact negation of the archive's already-evaluated "Payout Permanence Mix," so it is a mechanical sign relabeling of a known result rather than a new test.

target_name: Net Share Retirement Tilt Under Profit
rationale: Netting issuance out of the repurchase leg is a genuine and economically motivated single-variable change (option-heavy firms buy back while share count grows), though it overlaps meaningfully with the well-known net share issuance anomaly and with the archive's existing profitability×issuance-direction signals, so novelty is incremental rather than fundamental.

target_name: Repurchase Tilt Meets Free Cash Cover
rationale: Replacing the accrual-profitability weight with post-dividend cash cover is a substantive, non-cosmetic recombination of two distinct data inputs and the expression's natural direction matches the stated hypothesis, but its incremental value depends on a mix leg whose direction is already known from the archive, so the test is mostly about complementarity rather than a new mechanism.

The hypothesis and expression are internally consistent (a bounded non-negative payout-ratio rank scaling a two-sided margin change, so the signal concentrates in high-commitment payers), but the driving leg is the well-documented change-in-profitability effect and the payout ratio only modulates its amplitude, so a positive result may largely reflect the known base anomaly unless a low-payout control leg is also examined.

VOL of a strictly non-negative, right-skewed payout ratio scales mechanically with its level, so the "second-moment, orthogonal-to-label" claim is unsupported — the leg is likely a noisy proxy for payout magnitude — and the prior that payout instability predicts *higher* returns runs against both the standard smoothing/quality literature and the archive's own capital-structure-instability result.

Under US GAAP interest paid is already classified within operating cash flow, so SUB(oancf, xint) double-subtracts the interest charge and the "post-interest cash" leg does not compute what the hypothesis describes; absent that correction the leg reduces largely to oancf/at, making the signal a cash-profitability effect tilted toward high-interest firms rather than a clean commitment-versus-residual-cash test.
